text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: high GPU OOM rate in svc-inference-prod (prefill path). 30+ container restarts in last 5m. Severity: P2.

alex: I'm on it. pulling logs now.

ryan: @alex grabbing stack traces, looks like prefill spikes from some large-context customer sessions.

alex: seeing repeated error in container logs: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. tried to allocate 1.10 GiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total, 20.30 GiB free)`. also container restarts with SIGKILL shortly after prefill.

lee: paste of relevant log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T02:03:12Z] prefill_worker.cpp:142 allocate_kv_cache size=1363148800
[2026-03-15T02:03:12Z] runtime.cu:78 CUDA error: out of memory
[2026-03-15T02:03:12Z] container_manager: process exited (signal 9)
```

julia: Are these coming from a single node or many? node/instance-id: g4-prod-09 shows most restarts.

ryan: It's cluster-wide but noisy neighbor on g4-prod-09. Prefill token lengths jumped to ~120k tokens for some requests. Our prefill estimator didn't cap because client used large context window + long prompt.

alex: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Evict noisy containers on g4-prod-09, 2) Apply runtime hotpatch to cap prefill tokens for new requests, 3) Route traffic for that customer to a dedicated quota or smaller model. Which do we do now?

lee: Can do hotpatch quickly: set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=32768 and enable early-fail for requests > cap. I can push a canary to the node pool in ~6m.

deploy-bot: Rolling canary to pool: g4-prefill-canary (3/3 pods updated).

julia: I'm starting a kube drain+evict on g4-prod-09 for the noisy node to reduce restart storm. Command: `kubectl drain g4-prod-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

alex: Executed. Evictions underway. Monitoring pod restarts.

evan: Customer-impact: CS alerted. Affected customers: 2 mid-market accounts saw increased 5xxs and elevated latency for streaming responses. No data loss. I'll draft a status note.

ryan: Collected prefill histogram for last hour: median 3k tokens, p95 32k, p99.9 110k. The p99.999 spike aligns with that customer's job.

lee: Canary with PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS applied. Logs show new requests that exceed cap are rejected with 413 Payload Too Large and include guidance to client: `max_context_allowed=32768`. Example response header: `x-prefill-cap=32768`

alex: Good. After canary, node g4-prod-09 restarts reduced from 8/min to 0. Pod evictions completed.

deploy-bot: Canary successful. Promoting to 30% of pool.

ryan: Also applied a temporary routing rule to divert that customer's traffic to redwood-small-v1 (lower memory footprint) for up to 2h while they remediate.

evan: Sent interim customer message: "We're seeing large prefill windows from some of your requests that are triggering GPU memory limits; we've temporarily routed traffic to a smaller model and rate-limited huge contexts while we patch the runtime. No customer data exposed."

alex: Next actions: - Patch estimator to compute prefill token upper bound earlier in request pipeline - Add hard-server side cap with measurable metrics and dashboard - Add alert for prefill token spikes.

lee: I'll open a PR with the hotpatch and estimator fix. Patch notes include adding PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS env var and a preflight check in request_ingest: `if requested_prefill + context > PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS -> reject`.

ryan: For oncall handoff: I'm staying for now to monitor; @oncall-night you can pick up in 1h. If things are stable after promotion to pool, handoff then.

oncall-night: Acknowledged. I'll be ready for 02:50Z handoff.

alex: Postmortem draft points: cause = unbounded client-requested prefill for long-context session + insufficient runtime prefill caps; mitigation = emergency cap, node drain, customer routing; follow-ups = estimator fix, metrics + dashboard, add per-customer prefills quota.

evan: I'll coordinate customer follow-up and remediation guidance: suggest progressive batching on client side or using streaming prefill with KV checkpoints.

lee: quick note for engineering: command used to enforce cap on running pods (one-liner):
```
kubectl set env deployment/svc-inference PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=32768 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/svc-inference -n prod
```

alex: Monitoring charts: GPU OOMs dropped to near-zero after rollout and re-routing. p99 latency for generation returned to baseline within 12m.

julia: I'll keep the drain watch for 30m then bring node back with `kubectl uncordon g4-prod-09` if stable.

ryan: Logging action items in incident board: INC-5001. Owner assignments: lee (runtime patch), alex (postmortem), evan (customer comms), julia (node health).

evan: Customer update sent: "We applied temporary mitigations (routing + caps). We're working on a permanent runtime fix and will follow up with a timeline."

alex: closing notes: if anyone sees renewed OOMs tag #oncall. Great cross-team work. :thumbsup:
